HPV Vaccination & Series Rules

Series length and delayed doses

The decision point

Two rules apply independently. (1) Age at first dose sets the series length: under 15, 2 doses; ≥15 → 3 doses. Immunocompromised patients get 3 doses regardless of age. (2) Never restart a vaccine series; a delayed dose is simply given late. Minimum intervals matter; there is no maximum interval.

Scenario bank
  1. 12 yo F receiving her first HPV dose → Two doses
  2. 17 yo M receiving his first HPV dose → Three doses
  3. 13 yo M with HIV receiving his first dose → Three doses regardless of age
  4. 15 yo F who received one dose 14 months ago → Continue the series — never restart
  5. 28 yo F asking about catch-up vaccination → Shared decision-making through age 45
  6. 12 yo F who had dose one at age 11 and dose two 4 months later → Repeat the second dose → doses less than 5 months apart do not count
Bankable rules An interrupted vaccine series is not restarted; resume where you left off. A dose given 5 or more days before the minimum interval does not count and is repeated · catch-up HPV (human papillomavirus) vaccination is recommended through age 26, with shared decision-making at 27–45 · sexual activity, prior HPV exposure, and abnormal Pap results do not change the recommendation. Vaccinate anyway; the vaccine still protects against strains not yet acquired.
Transferable rule When lifestyle details appear alongside a guideline, check whether they actually change the algorithm. Usually they do not.
